drug_class: Enzyme replacement therapy (a man-made version of a natural body enzyme)
purpose: Asfotase alfa is used to treat a rare inherited condition called hypophosphatasia (HPP), which causes bones and teeth to be very weak and fragile due to a missing or poorly working enzyme. It helps the body properly mineralize (harden and strengthen) bones and teeth. This medicine is especially used in babies, children, and adults who developed HPP early in life.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes an enzyme called alkaline phosphatase that helps calcium and phosphorus get deposited into your bones to keep them strong. In HPP, this enzyme does not work well, so bones stay soft and weak. Asfotase alfa replaces this missing enzyme, allowing your bones to harden properly and become stronger over time.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions such as redness, bruising, pain, swelling, or hardening of the skin where the shot was given are very common. Some people may experience nausea, vomiting, fever, or headache. Skin discoloration or small lumps under the skin at the injection site can also occur with long-term use.
warnings: Some people may have serious allergic reactions including hives, difficulty breathing, or dizziness — seek emergency help right away if this happens. This medicine can cause kidney problems, including calcium buildup in the kidneys, so your doctor will monitor your kidneys regularly. Lipodystrophy (loss of fat tissue under the skin) can occur at injection sites, so it is important to rotate injection spots each time.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on your body weight and is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous). Most patients receive either 2 mg per kg of body weight three times per week, or 1 mg per kg of body weight six times per week. A healthcare provider will teach you or a caregiver how to give the injections at home.
